'''Yuri G. Zdesenko''' ({{langx|uk|Здесенко Юрій Георгійович}}); 6 October 1943 – 1 September 2004, was a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] known for a significant contribution to investigations of [[double beta decay]].

== Early life ==

Yuri G. Zdesenko was born on 6 October 1943 in [[Dmytrivka, Chernihiv Oblast|Dmytrivka]], [[Bakhmach Raion]], [[Chernihiv Oblast]], [[Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic]] of the [[Soviet Union]] to [[Soviet Army]] [[officer]] Georgy Zdesenko.

== Academic career ==

In 1970 Zdesenko was graduated from the Department of Physics of the [[Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv|T.G.Shevchenko Kyiv State University]]. He obtained degrees of [[Candidate of Sciences]] (Philosophy Doctor) in 1981 ([[Institute for Nuclear Research]], [[Moscow]], [[Soviet Union]]), [[Doktor nauk]] in 1990 ([[Institute for Nuclear Research of NASU|Institute for Nuclear Research]], [[Kyiv]], [[Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic]]) and the academic rank of [[Professor (highest academic rank)|Full Professor]] in 2000 ([[Institute for Nuclear Research of NASU|Institute for Nuclear Research]], [[Kyiv]], [[Ukraine]]). Taking into account his outstanding scientific achievements, Zdesnko was elected in 2003 a [[Corresponding Member]] of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]].

== Research ==

Zdesenko started researches in the Laboratory of Nuclear Physics of the T.G. Shevchenko Kyiv State University (1970–1971) and then in the Institute of Geochemistry and Physics of Minerals (1971–1980) where he dealt with [[neutron activation]] analysis of minerals and [[radiocarbon dating]]. At that time he became interested in double beta decay of atomic nuclei.<ref name = "1st-rev">Y.G. Zdesenko, ''[http://www.osti.gov/scitech/biblio/6189024 "Double β decay and conservation of lepton charge."]'' ''Sov. J. Part. Nucl. 11 (1980) 542.''</ref>

In 1980 he created the Laboratory for Low Background Measurements of the Special Construction Technological Center of the Institute for Nuclear Research of the Ukrainian Academy of Sciences (1980–1986) where searches for the double beta decay of <sup>130</sup>Te,<ref name = "130Te">Y.G. Zdesenko et al., ''[https://inis.iaea.org/search/searchsinglerecord.aspx?recordsFor=SingleRecord&RN=13667863 "Study of the double β decay of <sup>130</sup>Te"]'' '' Sov. J. Nucl. Phys. 32 (1980) 312.''</ref>  <sup>96</sup>Zr<ref name = "96Zr">Yu.G. Zdesenko et al., ''[https://inis.iaea.org/search/searchsinglerecord.aspx?recordsFor=SingleRecord&RN=13707256 "Search of <sup>96</sup>Zr neutrinoless double β-decay"]'' ''Izvestiya Akademii Nauk SSSR, Seriya Fizicheskaya 45 (1981) 1856.''</ref> and <sup>100</sup>Mo<ref name = "100Mo">Y.G. Zdesenko et al.,''[https://inis.iaea.org/search/searchsinglerecord.aspx?recordsFor=SingleRecord&RN=15032392 "Study on the double beta decay of <sup>100</sup>Mo"]'' ''Izvestiya Akademii Nauk SSSR, Seriya Fizicheskaya  28 (1983) 839.''</ref> were realized. In 1986 the laboratory was transformed to the Lepton Physics Department of the Institute for Nuclear Research (Kyiv, Ukraine).


In the early 1980s Zdesenko, supported by [[Bruno Pontecorvo]] (who was at that time head of the neutrino council of the [[Soviet Academy of Sciences]]), [[File:Yuri G. Zdesenko and Bruno Pontecorvo.jpg|thumb|Yuri G. Zdesenko with [[Bruno Pontecorvo]] on the background of the [[Mount Elbrus|Elbrus]] mountain, [[Baksan valley]], Russia, 1987]] initiated construction of the Solotvina Underground Laboratory in [[Solotvyno|Solotvina]], in [[Zakarpattia Oblast]] on the west of Ukraine. The Laboratory was located in a [[Salt mining|salt mine]] at a depth of 430 m. Low counting experiments were started  in the Solotvina laboratory in 1984. Investigations of rare nuclear [[alpha decay|alpha]] and [[beta decay]]s, searches for [[neutrinoless double beta decay]] of atomic nuclei were performed in the laboratory. The most valuable results obtained in the Solotvina Underground Laboratory are as following:
# the most stringent limits on neutrinoless double beta decay of <sup>116</sup>Cd obtained with the help of [[cadmium tungstate]] crystal [[scintillators]] enriched in [[isotope]] <sup>116</sup>Cd at 83%. One of the most stringent limits on the effective [[Majorana equation|Majorana]] [[neutrino]] mass was derived from the experiments;<ref name = "116Cd-1">F.A. Danevich et al., ''[https://inis.iaea.org/search/searchsinglerecord.aspx?recordsFor=SingleRecord&RN=20074438 "Search for 2β decay of <sup>116</sup>Cd with the help of a <sup>116</sup>CdWO<sub>4</sub> scintillator"]'' ''JETP Lett. 49 (1989) 476.''</ref><ref name = "116Cd-PLB">F.A. Danevich et al., ''[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/037026939401528K "The research of 2β decay of <sup>116</sup>Cd with enriched <sup>116</sup>CdWO<sub>4</sub> crystal scintillators"]'' ''Phys. Lett. B 344 (1995) 72.''</ref><ref name = "116Cd-final">F.A. Danevich et al., ''[http://journals.aps.org/prc/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevC.68.035501 "Search for 2β decay of cadmium and tungsten isotopes: Final results of the Solotvina experiment]'' ''Phys. Rev. Zdesenko et al., ''[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168900204021771 "Scintillation properties and radioactive contamination of CaWO<sub>4</sub> crystal scintillators"]'' ''Nucl. Instrum. Methods A 544 (2005) 553.''</ref> in particular, the cadmium tungstate crystal scintillators from enriched isotope cadmium 116 <ref name = "116Cd-1"/>

Zdesenko and his group have also contributed to searches for hypothetical decays [[Physics beyond the Standard Model|beyond the Standard Model]]: decays of nucleons into invisible channels,<ref name = "CaWO4" /><ref name = "invisible">R. Bernabei et al., ''[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269300011126 "Search for the nucleon and di-nucleon decay into invisible channels"]'' ''Phys. Lett. B 493 (2000) 12.''</ref> decays of electron with non-conservation of the electric charge,<ref name = "NCEC">P. Belli et al., ''[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269399010916 "Charge non-conservation restrictions from the nuclear levels excitation of <sup>129</sup>Xe induced by the electron's decay on the atomic shell"]'' ''Phys. Lett. B 465 (1999) 315.''</ref> charge-non-conserving β decays.<ref name = "CNC-73Ge">A.A. Klimenko et al., ''[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269302017240 "Experimental limit on the charge non-conserving β decay of <sup>73</sup>Ge"]'' ''Phys. Lett. B  535 (2002) 77.''</ref> Yuri G. Zdesenko is author or coauthor of above 300 scientific publications for which there are more than 1500 references in papers of other authors.
